title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21
lineage: Sony dynamic mics (balcony, 20' spread) > Sony 124 Cassette Deck > Norelco 120 normal bias tape > Susie Q > Tascam 122mk3 > Lucid ADA1000 A/D Converter > Tascam CDRW700 > EAC > Soundforge > CD Wave > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience recording captures a fiery early‑1970 Port Chester show with Viola Lee Blues blazing and the crowd’s energy intact.
ai_review.review: The tape, sourced from an audience recorder, is praised for its surprisingly clear vintage sound that lets listeners feel like they’re in the room. The performance shines especially on Viola Lee Blues, Walkin the Dog, Me & My Uncle and the rare Seven/Cumberland jam, delivering a fun, high‑energy early‑show vibe.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars, highlighting standout songs and a surprisingly good audience recording; only one reviewer notes modest sound issues, so both musical and technical quality are judged high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners repeatedly describe the tape as ‘nice sounding’, ‘best AUD source from 1970’, and “like it was recorded yesterday,” with only occasional mention of minor imperfections.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑show set is described as fun, informal and high‑energy with a solid mix of blues, rockers and rare jams; the audience’s presence adds to the charm.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for deep, primal psychedelic‑blues guitar work and intense playing on Viola Lee Blues.
